by: claude: tax back-fill 2015 onward, the four taxes the ten-year report reads (Spain, common regime: national rows and the 15 autonomous communities, Ceuta, Melilla)
note: Spain 2015 to 2025. National rows (savings scale for capital gains, solidarity tax, securities account) from PwC copies dated inside each year. The wealth tax is regional: one row per community per year from the tax agency's own yearly manual (AEAT Manual práctico de Patrimonio / Renta y Patrimonio; the 2015 regional addendum; the Ministry of Finance compilation for 2015 where a region set nothing). Each row stores the region's top band after any general rebate, the tax-free amount as the threshold, and the bands in the note. The four foral territories (Álava, Bizkaia, Gipuzkoa, Navarre) set their own wealth tax, savings scale and (Basque, from 2023) solidarity tax: their rows come from the yearly REAF Panorama de la Fiscalidad Autonómica y Foral; 2015 is unknown for them (gaps). Capital gains is marked as set per region, so every common-regime region carries the national savings scale and a foral year with no row stays unknown instead of borrowing the national rate.

jurisdictions.structure_note: The wealth tax (mínimo exento, scale, rebates) and inheritance tax are set by each of the 15 common-regime autonomous communities; Ceuta and Melilla apply the state rules. The Basque territories (Álava, Bizkaia, Gipuzkoa) and Navarra have their own foral tax systems, including the wealth tax and the tax on savings (capital gains). The solidarity tax on large fortunes (2022 onward) and the savings scale of the common regime are national.
